profile.reading:
365 Data Centers operates a colocation facility at 999 Frontier Rd in Bridgewater, New Jersey, a site the company markets as sitting on the Magic Mile fiber corridor roughly 40 miles west of New York City, a positioning meant to appeal to customers who want proximity to the New York metro market's connectivity and financial services activity without the real estate costs or congestion of a facility inside the city itself. 365 Data Centers is a Connecticut-based colocation operator that runs a network of facilities concentrated in the northeastern United States, and the Bridgewater site is one of its larger suburban New Jersey locations.

According to the company's own site, the Bridgewater facility totals 25,600 square feet of data center space, laid out with nearly 300 combination-locking cabinets along with custom cages and suites, on a 24 inch raised floor equipped with integrated fire and flood sensors. Roof access is available for customers who need to mount satellite equipment. On power, the company states 2.3 megawatts of power is currently installed with 20 megawatts total available on site for future expansion, backed by an N plus 1 UPS configuration and a 2N generator system with a 13,000 gallon onsite fuel tank rated for 72 hours of runtime. Cooling is stated at 300 tons of capacity with N plus 1 redundancy, using dry coolers and split condenser units in a hot aisle and cold aisle configuration with cold aisle containment, and fire suppression includes an FM 200 system in UPS rooms alongside a dry pipe pre-action system throughout the rest of the space.

The facility is audited to PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC 1, SOC 2, SSAE 18, and ISAE 3402 standards, and the company also cites an EcoVadis sustainability rating. Connectivity partners listed for the site include Altice, AT&T, Comcast, Crown Castle, Verizon, Zayo, and BAI Communications through its ZenFi Networks subsidiary, giving tenants a reasonably deep bench of carrier options without leaving the building. What the company does not publish for this site is a formal uptime tier classification or the year the building was originally constructed, though the level of detail 365 Data Centers provides for Bridgewater, spanning power, cooling, fire protection, and connectivity, is unusually thorough compared to many smaller regional operators.

reading.body:
This 25,600-square-foot facility in Bridgewater holds 2.3 MW of installed power with 20 MW more available on site, totaling 22.3 MW of announced capacity. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 22.3 MW of IT load would support roughly 560 racks of accelerator infrastructure. The campus ranks fifth among the five data centers in New Jersey with published power figures, accounting for approximately 20 percent of the state's total announced capacity of 111.3 MW.

The facility certifies to PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC 1, SOC 2, SSAE 18, and ISAE 3402 standards, qualifying it for regulated workloads in financial services and healthcare. No Tier classification is published. The operator does not publish whether the site has dedicated power infrastructure, whether it connects to the grid or on-site generation, or what constraints exist on reaching the stated 20 MW expansion figure.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities overall, but only five publish power capacity, making this site one of very few with transparent specifications in the state. Whether 22.3 MW of announced capacity in a northeastern market is material to AI scaling depends on whether that power is actually available and whether the operator intends to serve GPU-intensive workloads, neither of which is stated in the published record.
